## Process Economics and the importance of Carbon management

• Heat for the process can be produced by combusting 20-30% of the generated H2 resulting in no direct CO2 emissions for heat production • Net energy, thermal input are lower, and efficiency are higher with CMP than commercial SMR • H2 selling price is sensitive to C price. When C price is > $2/kg the process is more competitive than SMR • Catalyst recycle is not necessary when catalyst price is < $8/kg

• Catalyst price for Fe based catalyst in current work is projected to be < $3/kg • Ideal for integration with U.S. iron mining/beneficiation companies

Sensitivity of carbon selling price on H2 selling price and equivalent annual operating costs (EOAC). Comparison of NETL CMP with SMR based on preliminary systems analysis.

• J. Riley, R. Siriwardane, C. Atallah, R. • To integrate carbon products into the major markets, generated materials need to be proven and the properties characterized to ensure the product can offset another in the market. • Example of Carbon black (Largest Carbon Market Globally):

## • Number of different grades and uses accompanied by an ASTM

classification. • No such classification system exists for pyrolysis carbon products • Limited number pyrolysis technology startups. No info in the public

## domain of carbon product quality. • Challenging for a number of reasons:

## • Carbon products can occur in many different allotropes (graphitic

sheets, clusters, CNT, CNF, etc) and mixtures there of based on the technology (catalytic, plasma, thermal) and operating conditions. There is no routine or standard approach to assessing the allotrope and its distribution. And there isn’t yet a good handle (quantitively) on how process conditions/technology impact the product. • Properties can vary widely based on the allotrope. • Hinders progression to an ASTM classification

## • A standard approach to carbon product analysis requires leveraging

multiple complementary techniques to provide a detailed and reliable assessment. • Reliable product quantification will lead to avenues for marketability of the

## carbon and improve the viability of NG Pyrolysis

## • TGA/TPO Methods appear to provide a fast track approach to

## qualitatively assessing the carbon product distribution.

## • There is still substantial work underway to understand if the methods can be used to

differentiate characteristics within each allotrope (such as diameter, length, etc.) • Imaging based analyses are currently the only definitive approach to

## assess properties of allotropes. Targeted dispersion techniques are required to enable appropriate imaging.

## • Limitations exist with dispersion approaches and unzipping of carbon nano tubes.
